label: Quarterly results announcement
text:
PRESS RELEASE | Acme Dynamics Ltd (fictional sample)
Mumbai, 26 September 2026

Acme Dynamics reports Q2 FY27 results: revenue up 18%, EBITDA margin at 19.1%, net debt cut by Rs 310 crore

Acme Dynamics Ltd, a manufacturer of industrial automation systems, today announced results for the quarter ended 30 September 2026.

Consolidated revenue rose 18% year on year to Rs 4,320 crore, driven by strong demand for robotic assembly lines from electric-vehicle makers. EBITDA grew to Rs 825 crore, with the EBITDA margin improving to 19.1% from 17.4% a year earlier despite higher steel prices. Profit after tax was Rs 412 crore, up 22%.

The order book stood at a record Rs 11,600 crore, of which 42% comes from export customers in Europe and Southeast Asia. The company reduced net debt by Rs 310 crore during the quarter to Rs 1,050 crore, bringing net debt to EBITDA down to 0.9x.

Working capital days increased from 62 to 71 as the company built inventory for large EV-line contracts due for delivery in the second half. Management expects working capital to normalise by the end of the financial year.

"This quarter shows that our shift toward electric-vehicle automation is paying off," said Rohan Khanna, Managing Director and CEO. "We remain committed to our debt reduction targets and expect to be net-debt free by FY29."

The board approved an interim dividend of Rs 6 per share and capital expenditure of Rs 450 crore for a new robotics plant in Pune, expected to begin production in Q1 FY28.

Outlook: The company reiterated full-year revenue growth guidance of 15-17% and an EBITDA margin of 18.5-19.5%. Key risks include steel price volatility and delays in customer EV programmes.

18% revenue growth, a record order book and ₹310 crore less debt. Here's our Q2 FY27 in five numbers.

📈 ₹4,320 crore revenue, up 18% year on year
⚙️ 19.1% EBITDA margin, up from 17.4% despite higher steel prices
💰 ₹412 crore profit after tax, up 22%
📦 ₹11,600 crore order book, a record, with 42% from exports
🏦 Net debt down to ₹1,050 crore, just 0.9x EBITDA

The story behind the numbers is electric vehicles. EV makers are automating faster than ever, and our robotic assembly lines are right at the centre of that shift.

We're also investing ahead of demand, with ₹450 crore committed to a new robotics plant in Pune, expected to start production in Q1 FY28.

"This quarter shows that our shift toward electric-vehicle automation is paying off," said Rohan Khanna, our Managing Director and CEO. "We remain committed to our debt reduction targets and expect to be net-debt free by FY29."

Thank you to our teams, customers and partners who made this quarter possible.
